ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Approximately 45:55 ratio of high-intensity (white) pixels to low-intensity (black) pixels across the visible ventral fluke surface.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Large contiguous high-intensity white regions occupy the superior-lateral sections of both lobes. A dominant low-intensity black region covers the central notch area and inferior margins, with fine-grained black mottling and vertical striations interspersed throughout the white fields.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Narrow U-shaped central depression with a calculated pixel angle of approximately 32 degrees and a depth relative to the lobal apex of ~12%.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: The left lobe trailing edge exhibits high-amplitude, irregular serrations with three distinct macro-notches. The right lobe trailing edge displays lower-amplitude, high-frequency oscillations and micro-serrations.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Gentle convex curvature from the median notch extending to the lateral tips, with an increasing upward slope toward the distal extremities.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Clusters of high-intensity, roughly circular pixel groups (barnacle-like structures) are concentrated at the extreme distal tips of both lobes, with higher density on the right tip.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Numerous low-intensity vertical and diagonal linear disruptions (rake marks) are detected across the white pigmented regions of both the left and right lobes.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: A prominent V-shaped indentation/trauma mark is visible on the inner trailing edge of the left lobe, adjacent to the median notch. White calcified clusters are present on the leading edges of the lateral tips.
other_distinctive_markers: Highly dense concentration of dark, fine-line vertical striations on the far lateral white patch of the left lobe.
